lessonDetails.title: The Plagues of Egypt
lessonDetails.scriptureDisplay: Exodus 7–10 (first nine plagues; first plague reviewed from previous lesson)

bigIdeas.text: The Lord is the ONE TRUE God.

originalCurriculumVerse.text: For the Lord your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, the mighty, and the awesome God...

sourceFiles.note: The lesson covers the first nine plagues; there is no accompanying ODP. The original memory verse is an ESV excerpt of Deuteronomy 10:17a.

storyNotes.cleanText: God turned the water of Egypt into blood.
God covered the land of Egypt with frogs.
God turned the dust of Egypt into gnats.
God sent swarms of flies into Egypt, but spared Goshen.
The livestock of the Egyptians died, but the Israelites’ animals survived.
God sent painful boils on Egyptian people and animals.
God sent a severe hailstorm to Egypt but spared Goshen.
God sent locusts to eat the plants left after the hail.
God covered Egypt in darkness for three days, but Israel had light.

questions.question: But when they spoke to Pharaoh, the stubborn king of Egypt, what did he say?
questions.answer: “I don’t know the Lord God of Israel and I’m not letting my slaves go!”

questions.question: What was plague #1?
questions.answer: God turned the water of Egypt into blood.

questions.question: After seeing the power of the Lord, what did Pharaoh say?
questions.answer: He wouldn’t let the people go.

questions.question: What was plague #2?
questions.answer: God covered the land with frogs.

questions.question: After the Lord punished Egypt with a plague of frogs, what did Pharaoh say?
questions.answer: He said they could go if Moses prayed to send them away; when the frogs left, he changed his mind.
questions.notes: Footnote marker after question in original ODT points to Story Sheet Instructions.

questions.question: What was plague #3?
questions.answer: God turned the dust to gnats.

questions.question: After the Lord God punished Egypt with a plague of gnats, what did Pharaoh say?
questions.answer: He wouldn’t let God’s people go.

questions.question: What was plague #4?
questions.answer: God covered the land with flies.

questions.question: Why didn’t they have flies?
questions.answer: That’s where God’s people lived.

questions.question: After the Lord God punished Egypt with a plague of flies, what did Pharaoh say?
questions.answer: “If you pray for the flies to leave, I’ll let you go”; when the flies left, Pharaoh changed his mind.

questions.question: What was plague #5?
questions.answer: Their animals died.

questions.question: Why?
questions.answer: That’s where God’s people lived.
questions.notes: Context-dependent question: Goshen/Israelite animals spared, or no hail in Goshen, depending on location.

questions.question: After the Lord God punished Egypt with a plague of dead livestock, what did Pharaoh say?
questions.answer: He wouldn’t let them go.

questions.question: What was plague #6?
questions.answer: People were covered with boils.

questions.question: After the Lord God punished Egypt with a plague of boils, what did Pharaoh say?
questions.answer: He would not let the people go.

questions.question: What was plague #7?
questions.answer: A hailstorm.

questions.question: Why?
questions.answer: That’s where God’s people lived.
questions.notes: Context-dependent question: Goshen/Israelite animals spared, or no hail in Goshen, depending on location.

questions.question: What did Pharaoh have to say about this?
questions.answer: The lesson directs the teacher to read the answer next.
questions.notes: Teacher transition before reading Scripture; not a factual stand-alone worksheet item.

questions.question: After the Lord God punished Egypt with a plague of hail, what did Pharaoh say?
questions.answer: He asked Moses to pray that the hail would stop; when it did, Pharaoh changed his mind.

questions.question: What was plague #8?
questions.answer: Locusts.

questions.question: What was Pharaoh’s response to this?
questions.answer: The lesson directs the teacher to read the answer next.
questions.notes: Teacher transition before reading Scripture; not a factual stand-alone worksheet item.

questions.question: After the Lord God punished Egypt with a plague of locusts, what did Pharaoh say?
questions.answer: He asked Moses to pray that the locusts would leave; when they did, he changed his mind.

questions.question: What was plague #9?
questions.answer: Darkness.

questions.question: Why?
questions.answer: God’s people lived there.
questions.notes: Context-dependent question: Goshen/Israelite animals spared, or no hail in Goshen, depending on location.

questions.question: What did Pharaoh do with all this dark?
questions.answer: The lesson directs the teacher to read the answer next.
questions.notes: Teacher transition before reading Scripture; not a factual stand-alone worksheet item.

questions.question: After the Lord God punished Egypt with a plague of darkness, what did Pharaoh say?
questions.answer: You can leave, but don’t take your animals; when Moses said no, Pharaoh changed his mind.

questions.question: So how does the story of the plagues of Egypt teach us, strengthen us, encourage us, or give us hope?
questions.answer: Various responses.

questions.question: But Pharaoh and the Egyptians?
questions.answer: They worshiped many gods they thought were real.

questions.question: Can you guess which Egyptian “god” would be the target of God’s final plague?
questions.answer: Pharaoh himself.

questions.question: What does that mean?
questions.answer: That God is the God in charge of all the other gods (who don’t really exist anyway) and he is the Lord (or king) in charge of all the other lords (or kings).
questions.notes: Source contains two separate questions in the same paragraph.

questions.question: How did God show that he was the God in charge of the “gods” Egypt worshiped?
questions.answer: He sent plagues to show his power.
questions.notes: Source contains two separate questions in the same paragraph.

facts.statement: God turned the water of the Nile into blood.
God spared Goshen from swarms of flies.
The Israelites’ livestock died in the fifth plague.
God caused painful boils on Egyptian people.
The hailstorm struck the Israelites in Goshen.
Locusts ate plants that survived the hail.
The darkness over Egypt lasted seven days.
Pharaoh asked Moses to pray for the frogs to leave.
Pharaoh freed Israel after the locusts left.
Israel’s homes had light during Egypt’s darkness.
The Israelites were stuck in darkness for three days.
The lesson teaches that the Lord is the one true God.

clues.text: I prayed for Pharaoh and warned him about the plagues.
I held out my staff as God sent early plagues.
I was the stubborn king of Egypt and would not let Israel leave.
We were God’s people living in Goshen, spared from several plagues.

keyPhrases.text: The Lord is the ONE TRUE God.
God showed His power through the plagues of Egypt.
Pharaoh continued to refuse to release the Israelites.
God spared His people from several of Egypt’s plagues.
The Lord’s power is greater than the gods Egypt worshiped.
The Lord is the one true God.

theologicalApplications.text: The plagues showed Egypt that the Lord alone is the true God.
Pharaoh kept refusing to release Israel even when he saw God’s power.
The lesson contrasts the Lord with the Egyptian gods whom the people worshiped.
The lesson connects God’s power in Egypt with His sending Jesus to rescue people from sins.
The children are invited to confess in prayer that the Lord is the one true God.

finishStory.markedParagraph: God sent [BLOOD] as the first plague, turning Egypt’s water red. Next, [FROGS] filled the land, but Pharaoh changed his [mind] after they went away. Then dust turned into [GNATS], and swarms of [FLIES] filled Egypt while Goshen, were the Israelites lived, was spared. In the fifth plague, the Egyptians’ [LIVESTOCK] died, but the Israelites’ animals survived. Moses scattered ashes, and painful [BOILS] broke out on people and animals. Next, a great storm of [HAIL] struck Egypt, but not the Israelites. The eighth plague brought [LOCUSTS], which ate what was left after the hail. For the ninth plague, thick [DARKNESS] covered Egypt for three days, but the Israelites had [light]. Despite these plagues, Pharaoh still refused to let God’s people [go].

reviewFlags.text: This lesson teaches plagues 1–9 only. Plague 1 is a recap from the prior lesson; do not add the tenth plague or Passover to printed activities.
Source ESV Deuteronomy 10:17a differs from proposed BSB excerpt. Confirm BSB selection, excerpt ending and punctuation using the Review Studio; Scripture-rights clearance remains unapproved.
Approve six newly composed false statements. Ensure none are misleading, especially Goshen and Pharaoh’s changing responses.
Review both suggested incorrect choices for each of the six Multiple Choice questions.
Review four concise scene prompts and six complete Draw the Story captions. The latter reuse Story Order wording.
Approve the plausible but unrelated Odd Words and Checkboxes items: Giant, Sling, Harp, Ladder, Scroll.
Review eight deliberately incorrect words/phrases and all corrections in Circle Mistakes.
The source Story Notes are nine brief plague labels, not narrative sentences. Review adapted chronological captions and Finish the Story narrative.
Review adapted references to Egyptian gods and the source’s claim that plagues defeated named gods; do not present these comparative statements as independently verified historical facts.
Review age-appropriate references to livestock death, illness, judgment and the deferred tenth plague.
Schema-valid word clues are not proof a crossword grid can be generated. Run the actual crossword builder.
Run all 27 module preflight checks and all three numbered worksheet presets in the real application; these tests were not run here.
The source contains many nearly identical Pharaoh questions; all have been preserved, but only a small distinct set is used for prepared Multiple Choice.
Big Idea capitalization normalized to “The Lord is the ONE TRUE God.” following the updated God capitalization rule.
